title: monitoring.py router never registered — 5 endpoints unreachable

title: Fallback error handler defined inline — hides import failure silently

A missing `enhanced_error_handling` module produces no startup warning; the fallback `validate_stock_symbol` regex is simpler than the real implementation, leading to different validation behaviour.

title: health.py uses synchronous SQLAlchemy engine — blocks async event loop
description: `health.py:8` imports `engine` (sync) from `backend.utils.database` and `get_db_sync`. The `readiness_check` endpoint uses `with engine.connect() as conn:` — a blocking synchronous database call inside an async FastAPI endpoint. Under load this blocks the entire event loop thread for the duration of the DB query.
recommendation: Replace with async DB check: `async with db_manager.get_session() as session: await session.execute(text("SELECT 1"))` as done in monitoring.py:51-52.
acceptance_test_hint: `GET /api/health/readiness` does not block other concurrent requests during the DB check (load test with 50 concurrent requests)

recommendation: Move `handle_secure_client_message` into `backend/services/websocket_service.py`. Update docstring to accurately describe the file's responsibility.
acceptance_test_hint: `websocket.py` line count < 150; `websocket_service.py` contains the message handler

title: MiddlewarePriority NORMAL(5000) conflicts with REQUEST_SIZE(5000) — ambiguous ordering
description: `MiddlewarePriority.NORMAL = 5000` and `MiddlewarePriority.REQUEST_SIZE = 5000` have the same integer value. Python sort is stable so their order is determined by registration order, but this is fragile and not documented.
recommendation: Assign NORMAL a unique value (e.g. 5500 or 4500) or remove NORMAL as it is not used in main.py.
acceptance_test_hint: `list(set(m.value for m in MiddlewarePriority))` length equals `len(MiddlewarePriority)`

title: RecommendationService duplicates 100% of two unused mixins
description: `RecommendationService` is declared as `class RecommendationService:` (no base class). Yet `recommendation_crud.py:49` defines `RecommendationCrudMixin` with 11 methods and `recommendation_analysis.py:31` defines `RecommendationAnalysisMixin` with 6 async methods — every one of those 17 methods is also independently re-implemented (cut-and-pasted) inside `RecommendationService`. SEC disclosure constants are defined in BOTH `recommendation_service.py:25-51` and `recommendation_crud.py:23-46`. `grep -rn "RecommendationCrudMixin\
recommendation: RecommendationAnalysisMixin" backend/` confirms zero non-mixin-file consumers. Any future bug-fix to one copy will silently fail to apply to the other. The N+1 batch fix (F-09-002 cross-link) is currently doubled — both `recommendation_service.py:288` and `recommendation_analysis.py:110` contain identical `get_top_stocks`/`get_bulk_price_history` calls.
acceptance_test_hint: Either (a) make `RecommendationService(RecommendationCrudMixin, RecommendationAnalysisMixin)` and delete the in-class duplicates, OR (b) delete the two mixin files entirely. Option (a) reduces `recommendation_service.py` from 1234 → ~250 LOC. Pick (a) if mixin tests in `backend/tests/` exist; pick (b) if not. | After fix: `wc -l backend/services/recommendation_service.py` < 350; `pytest backend/tests/test_recommendation*.py` all pass; `grep -c "def generate_sec_disclosure\ | def generate_sample_recommendation\ | def generate_ml_powered_recommendations" backend/services/recommendation_*.py` returns exactly one definition per method across the three files.

title: aiohttp ClientSession closed before WebSocket can be used
description: `connect()` does `async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as session: self.websocket = await session.ws_connect(...); ... self._receive_task = asyncio.create_task(self._receive_loop())` and then returns. The function returns from inside the `async with` — Python immediately exits the context manager and `session.__aexit__` is called, which closes the session and (per aiohttp semantics) the websocket created from it. The receive loop runs once, gets `WSMsgType.CLOSED`, breaks, calls `_handle_connection_error`, and reconnects in an infinite loop. Real-time price streaming via Finnhub will never function.
recommendation: Promote `self._session = aiohttp.ClientSession()` to an instance attribute initialised in `__init__`, and close it in `disconnect()`. Do not use `async with` for a long-lived session. Pattern: `self._session = aiohttp.ClientSession(); self.websocket = await self._session.ws_connect(...)`.
acceptance_test_hint: After fix: integration test connects to a stub Finnhub websocket, sends one trade message, receives it via callback within 1 s without reconnect. `aiohttp.ClientSession` lifetime equals the `FinnhubWebSocketClient` lifetime.

title: Async scheduler is wired but every body is commented out
description: `main.py:92-93` calls `start_scheduler()` in lifespan startup. `scheduler.py:48-95` defines three coroutines `_periodic_market_data`, `_periodic_portfolio_update`, `_periodic_alert_check` — each has its production line commented (`# In production: celery_app.send_task(...)`) and only logs at DEBUG and sleeps. Operators see "AsyncScheduler started" in logs and assume background tasks are running, but in reality nothing fires unless an external Celery beat process is also running (which is not started by `start.sh dev` in many configurations). Combined with `data_pipeline.py:29` referencing the non-existent `backend.config.celery_config` module, the task subsystem has multiple broken entry points.
recommendation: Choose one: (a) delete `scheduler.py` and rely solely on Celery beat (canonical for production); document that beat MUST run; (b) implement the scheduler to actually call `celery_app.send_task(...)` and remove the comments. Option (a) is preferred — the dual-system creates ambiguity.
acceptance_test_hint: After fix: either `scheduler.py` is deleted and `main.py:92-93` removed; OR `_periodic_market_data` actually calls `celery_app.send_task` and an integration test verifies that scheduling a 5-second interval enqueues a task.

Document the decision in `docs/architecture/`. Current state misleads new contributors who think DDD is an active pattern. | After fix: either (a) `MarketDataServiceImpl(MarketDataContract)` exists and is used by the API, or (b) `backend/domain/` is deleted and `test_domain_contracts.py` is removed; `find backend/domain -name "*.py" \ | wc -l` returns 0.

title: `get_bulk_price_history` called with timezone-naive `datetime.now().date()`
description: Both copies pass `start_date=datetime.now().date() - timedelta(days=90)` and `end_date=datetime.now().date()`. `datetime.now()` returns the local-machine timezone. In a UTC-deployed container with a user in another zone (or running near midnight UTC), the date range can be off by a day, missing the most recent close. Almost the entire codebase uses `datetime.now(timezone.utc)` — these two sites are the holdouts (cross-references F-11-006 from scope 11).
recommendation: Replace with `datetime.now(timezone.utc).date()`. Also import `timezone` (already imported at line 9) and use it consistently.
acceptance_test_hint: After fix: `grep -nE "datetime\.now\(\)\.(date\(\) | date\b)" backend/services/recommendation_*.py` returns 0 hits.

title: New N+1 query in `_build_position_list` after the recommendations N+1 fix
description: For every position in a portfolio detail call, `_build_position_list` does `stock_info = await stock_repository.get_by_symbol(db_pos.symbol, session=db)`. A 30-stock portfolio = 30 DB round-trips per detail page load. Same pattern that the INTEGRATION_SUMMARY claimed was eliminated for recommendations.
recommendation: Pre-fetch in bulk: collect all `db_pos.symbol`s, call `stock_repository.get_by_symbols_bulk(symbols, session=db)` (add this method to the repo if it doesn't exist), build a dict `{symbol: stock}`, then look up.
acceptance_test_hint: After fix: integration test on a 30-position portfolio shows query count for `compute_portfolio_detail` ≤ 6 (was ~36). `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` of the bulk `IN (...)` query is faster than the loop.

title: Standalone Celery `app` references missing config module
description: `app = Celery('data_pipeline')` then `app.config_from_object('backend.config.celery_config')`. `find backend/config -name "celery_config*"` returns 0 hits. The line will raise `ImportError` if `data_pipeline.py` is imported as a Celery worker entry point. The module also defines its own `beat_schedule` (line 423-) parallel to `celery_app.py`, indicating two competing beat configs.
recommendation: Either: (a) delete `data_pipeline.py` and merge any unique tasks into `data_tasks.py` under the canonical `celery_app`; or (b) create `backend/config/celery_config.py` and document why `data_pipeline.py` needs a separate Celery instance.
acceptance_test_hint: After fix: `python -c "from backend.tasks.data_pipeline import app; app.conf"` does not raise; OR file deleted and `grep -rn "data_pipeline" backend/` returns no production refs.

description: `task_config.py` defines `TaskPriority(IntEnum)`, `CELERY_TASK_QUEUES` with priorities (critical/high/default/low/background), `CELERY_TASK_ROUTES`, `apply_task_config` helper. `grep -rn "from backend.tasks.task_config\
recommendation: task_config" backend/ \
acceptance_test_hint: grep -v __pycache__ \ | grep -v test` returns 0 production hits. The actual queue config used by `celery_app.py:99-115` is a different, simpler scheme (default/high_priority/low_priority/data_ingestion/analysis/notifications). Two competing schemes; the more sophisticated one is dead. | If `task_config` is the intended future direction, migrate `celery_app.py` to import from it and delete the inline queue definitions. If not, delete `task_config.py` and update `backend/tests/test_task_optimization.py`. | After fix: only one source of `TaskPriority` and queue config; integration test verifies tasks are routed to expected queues.

title: Technical analysis runs on synthetic random data, not real prices
description: `run_technical_analysis(ticker, depth)` does `np.random.seed(hash(ticker) % (2**31))` and then synthesises 250 days of fake OHLCV from `np.random.normal(0.0005, 0.02, n)`. The deterministic seeding hides the fact that this is NOT real market data — every call returns a stable but completely fabricated price series for the ticker. The `TechnicalAnalysisEngine.analyze_stock(df)` then computes "real" technical indicators on synthetic input, returning a `composite_score` to the user.
recommendation: Replace synthetic prices with a real fetch from `price_repository.get_price_history(ticker, ...)`. Fall back to `NotImplementedError` rather than synthetic data when prices are unavailable.
acceptance_test_hint: After fix: `grep -n "np.random.seed\ | np.random.normal" backend/services/agents_service.py` returns 0 hits; integration test asserts the technical-engine result for AAPL on a fixed date matches the engine output on real fixture data (not deterministic-random).

title: Duplicate SEC disclosure constants drift risk
description: `RECOMMENDATION_MODEL_VERSION = "1.0.0"` and `RECOMMENDATION_MODEL_TRAINING_DATE = "2025-12-15"` are defined identically in both files. SEC compliance text (`SEC_RISK_WARNING`, `SEC_METHODOLOGY_DISCLOSURE_TEMPLATE`, `SEC_LIMITATIONS_STATEMENT`) is also duplicated character-for-character. Any compliance update touching one file silently leaves the other emitting stale wording.
recommendation: Move constants to `backend/services/sec_disclosures.py` (new file) and import in both modules — or fix F-02-001 first, which deletes the duplication.
acceptance_test_hint: After fix: only one definition site for each constant; `grep -c "SEC_RISK_WARNING =" backend/services/` returns 1.

recommendation: ComprehensiveStockFetcher" backend/` returns ONLY the file itself and one stale entry in `docs/architecture/CODEBASE_ARCHITECTURE_MAP.md:369`. Not a Celery task (no `@celery_app.task` decorator), not registered in beat schedule, not called from any service.

title: Duplicated in-memory TTL cache implementations
description: Two services each define `_mem_cache: Dict[str, Tuple[float, object]]`, `_*_cache_get`, `_*_cache_set`, with TTL only differing (900 s vs 60 s). Identical patterns, no shared util. Fragile under multi-process Celery (each worker has its own dict; cache misses depending on which worker handles request).
recommendation: Extract to `backend/utils/local_ttl_cache.py` (or use existing `backend/utils/cache.py::LRUCache`). Both services import it.
acceptance_test_hint: After fix: `grep -rn "_mem_cache\ | _price_cache" backend/services/` returns 0 hits; both services import from utils.

title: `day_change` calculation uses heuristic `* 0.01` magic number
description: `day_change += position.quantity * (price_update.close - position.average_cost) * 0.01`. The 0.01 multiplier is unexplained — it converts the gain-vs-cost into an approximate daily change but the math is incorrect (close - average_cost is total gain since entry, not day change). The day_change passed to clients is a hand-tuned guess.
recommendation: Use `price_update.change` (per-share daily change) directly: `day_change += position.quantity * price_update.change`. The `RealtimePriceService` already returns `change` field (see `realtime_price_service.py:42`).
acceptance_test_hint: After fix: integration test with known prices verifies `day_change` matches `Σ qty × per-share-change`.

title: `calculate_rsi` and `calculate_macd` are stub `return None`
description: Despite their bodies being a single `return None`, both are exported from the module and may be imported by tests. They are misleading — the file has helper logic for fetching real RSI/MACD via `alpha_vantage_client.get_rsi(...)` (lines 116-127) but the local stubs invite callers to use the broken pure-Python version.

acceptance_test_hint: After fix: `grep -nE "def calculate_(rsi\ | macd)" backend/services/analysis_service.py` returns 0 hits OR functions return real values for sample inputs.

title: Sector approximation uses `pos.symbol[:2]`
description: `unique_sectors = len(set(pos.symbol[:2] for pos in positions))` uses the first 2 chars of the ticker as a sector proxy. This bears no relation to actual sector and produces nonsense (e.g., AAPL and AAL both `AA`; MSFT and META don't match). The diversification bonus computed from this is meaningless.
recommendation: Read `pos.stock.sector` (already available via repo). If positions are domain models without `sector`, look up via `stock_repository.get_by_symbols_bulk(...)` (combine with F-02-007).
acceptance_test_hint: After fix: `unique_sectors` matches the count of distinct `Stock.sector` values for the position list.

title: Module-level engine singletons not thread-safe
description: `_fundamental_engine`, `_technical_engine`, `_sentiment_engine` use `global` and a None-check. In a multi-thread test runner or under FastAPI's threadpool fallback, two requests racing the lazy init can each construct a separate engine.
recommendation: Wrap with `asyncio.Lock` or use `functools.lru_cache(maxsize=None)`. Or instantiate at module import time.
acceptance_test_hint: After fix: concurrent-stress test does not produce two engine instances.

title: Two scheduling systems both documented as canonical

title: Bare `except:` clauses swallow all exceptions
description: 13 bare `except:` clauses (no exception type). Catches `KeyboardInterrupt`, `SystemExit`, `GeneratorExit`. Hides bugs and prevents shutdown.
recommendation: Replace each with `except Exception:` minimum, or narrower types based on the protected operation (e.g., `except (json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError):`). Add `logger.exception(...)` if not already present.
acceptance_test_hint: `ruff check --select E722` returns 0 hits in `backend/utils/`.

title: Pervasive timezone-naive `datetime.now()`
description: Throughout cost monitors, circuit breakers, cache warming, etc. `datetime.now()` is used without tz, mixing with timezone-aware `datetime.now(timezone.utc)` in `structured_logging.py`. Causes subtle bugs in serialization, persistence, and inter-service correlation.
recommendation: Project-wide replacement to `datetime.now(timezone.utc)` (or use `time.monotonic()` for durations). Add a `ruff` rule (`DTZ005`) to lock it in.

title: Comprehensive but largely-unwired error handling system

title: Large modules exceed project's 800-line "max" guideline
description: Project rule (`.claude/rules/coding-style.md`) says 200-400 typical, 800 max. These three modules (and 4 others) exceed it. `risk_manager.py` already extracts `var_utils`/`risk_metrics`/`risk_stress` (good); finish the job.
recommendation: Continue the extraction pattern: split `portfolio_optimizer.py` into `optimizer_core/constraints/metrics`; split `resilient_pipeline.py` by stage.
acceptance_test_hint: All `backend/utils/*.py` ≤ 800 LOC.

title: Test imports a module that has no production users
description: `tests/test_cache_warming.py:10` imports `backend.utils.cache_warmer.CacheWarmer` — a class with no production callers. The test asserts on hard-coded internals (`top_stocks == 20`, `etf_list == 5`). Misleads coverage metrics.
recommendation: After F-11-002 deletion, remove this test.
acceptance_test_hint: `pytest backend/tests/test_cache_warming.py` fails with collection error → after fix, file is gone and suite still passes.

title: `__init__.py` only re-exports two of 60 utilities
description: Re-exports just `RiskManager` and `PortfolioOptimizer`. Implies a public API but is incomplete. Most callers import from submodules directly, so the re-export is rarely used.
recommendation: Either (a) remove the re-exports and document that submodules are the API, or (b) build a deliberate public surface. Decide consistently.
acceptance_test_hint: `backend/utils/__init__.py` is documented and consistent with import patterns elsewhere in the codebase.

title: Prior cites main.py line numbers that no longer exist
description: §4 cites `main.py` lines 195-223 for global handlers; they were extracted to `backend/middleware/error_handler.py`. Anyone reading the prior is misled.
recommendation: Replace the prior with a pointer to this audit report, or annotate it with an "ARCHIVED — see audits/2026-04" note. (Out of scope for this read-only audit; flagged for synthesis.)
acceptance_test_hint: Prior file has visible deprecation banner OR is moved into `docs/archive/`.

title: Hard dependency on `structlog` even in code paths that only use stdlib logging
description: Top-level `import structlog`. If the package is missing in a slim deployment, even basic logging breaks.
recommendation: Make `structlog` optional at module level with a try/import; fall back to stdlib in non-structured paths.
acceptance_test_hint: Module imports successfully when `structlog` is uninstalled (verified in a slim venv).

title: `from .exceptions import *` (wildcard import)
description: Wildcard imports muddle the namespace and surface name conflicts.
recommendation: Replace with explicit imports of the names actually used.
acceptance_test_hint: `ruff check --select F403` returns 0 hits in `backend/utils/`.

title: Top-of-file docstring says "Utility modules for the investment analysis platform" — and that's it
description: No mention of structure, conventions, or the deliberate (vs accidental) re-exports.
recommendation: Either expand or remove (per F-11-014).
acceptance_test_hint: Single coherent module-level docstring.

title: Anonymized IP uses `XXX.XXX` (uppercase)
description: Cosmetic; some downstream parsers expect numeric `0` or RFC `*`.
recommendation: Use `0.0` or `*.*` per a documented convention.
acceptance_test_hint: Document the chosen convention in a docstring; existing tests still pass.
